Spec: `docs/epics/csv-export/spec.md`

## What to build

One end-to-end test that walks the CSV export feature the way an operator uses it: request an export, download it, run it again, keep one copy, delete the other. It runs over real storage with a fake only at the object-store edge, and checks at the end that the deleted export's database row and its CSV file are both gone.

Then the failures that belong to no single ticket: the worker killed mid-export, the bucket credential revoked between runs, and a disk that cannot be written to. Each must fail closed: the operator sees a message that says what to do, and no export visible to her is missing its file.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The end-to-end test runs the full loop over real storage and passes
- [ ] After a delete, both the row and the CSV file are gone
- [ ] A worker killed mid-export never leaves an export that downloads nothing; a file with no row is tolerated
- [ ] A revoked credential or an unwritable disk is reported in plain words and leaves nothing half-visible
- [ ] Tests check observable behaviour, not call sequences

## Sequencing

The row is written before the file, so an interruption between the two can leave a file with no row. That is recoverable and is not asserted against. The inverse, a row whose file is absent, must be unreachable.

## Blocked by

- #57
- #85
- #86
